name: Aurthohin

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Funk, jazz fusion, and progressive metal traditions (general)
global_influences.evidence: Sumon's personal interest in slap bass steered Aurthohin's sound toward funk-rock, and influences spanning funk, jazz fusion and progressive metal are evident across the band's catalogue — a comparatively rare combination within Bangladeshi rock, distinguishing Aurthohin from straighter hard-rock or metal peers.

local_adaptation_notes: Aurthohin grew directly out of frontman Sumon's earlier solo project Sumon O Aurthohin, recorded while he was still a member of Warfaze — making the band a direct genealogical branch of Bangladesh's heavy metal pioneers that pivoted toward a funk/jazz-fusion-inflected alternative rock sound; the band is also credited with actively supporting underground rock/metal acts, positioning it as an infrastructural as well as musical influence on the scene.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1998): formed by Sumon (fresh from Warfaze), Tonmoy Rahman, Ponir and Rumi Rahman. Breakthrough period (2000): debut album Trimatrik, one of the earliest hard rock records in Bangladesh, established the band nationally. Later period: eight to nine studio albums released over time, with the sound progressively incorporating progressive metal, groove metal and funk-rock elements as Sumon's slap-bass-driven sensibility matured; Sumon remains the sole continuous founding member.
concert_culture_notes: Notable for its role supporting and mentoring underground rock/metal bands in Bangladesh, suggesting a concert-culture role beyond its own headline shows — functioning as a connective node within the live metal/rock scene ecosystem.
listener_community_notes: Considered one of the pioneering bands of Bangladeshi alternative rock; its funk/jazz-fusion hybridity attracts listeners overlapping both the metal scene (via Sumon's Warfaze lineage) and more experimental alternative/progressive audiences.
